Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jamie Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q4 2023 results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer; and Rachel Patel, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Jamie, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q4 2023. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional fund performance, robust market trends, and strategic product innovations. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q4 2023. Our revenue was $4.2 billion, representing a 20% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, resilient fee rates, and accelerated net inflows. Our expenses were $2.6 billion, resulting in net income of $1.4 billion. We continue to manage our expenses prudently while investing in high-ROI areas like technology and distribution.

Let me unpack our net flows, which remain a cornerstone of our organic growth. For the quarter, we recorded net inflows of $12.5 billion, bringing our full-year total to $45.2 billion—a robust 28% increase year-over-year and our strongest annual performance since 2021. This propelled ending AUM to a record $1.45 trillion, up 14% from year-end 2022. Long-term net flows, excluding ETFs and cash equivalents, came in at $9.8 billion for the quarter, reflecting sustained demand across retail, high-net-worth, and institutional channels.

Fund performance has been our most potent attractor. Our active equity strategies delivered exceptional results, with the Apex Global Equity Fund generating 18.2% net returns for the year, outperforming its MSCI World benchmark by 420 basis points. This earned us 14 first-quartile Lipper rankings across core large-cap growth and value composites, up from nine last year. Institutional clients like defined benefit pensions and sovereign wealth funds contributed $4.2 billion of quarterly inflows from performance-related mandates, including a $1.1 billion commitment from a major Nordic pension fund citing our consistent outperformance in attribution reports.

In fixed income, amid rate volatility, our multi-sector bond strategies excelled. The Apex Core Plus Bond Fund returned 6.8% annualized, beating the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate by 110 basis points, thanks to tactical overweights in investment-grade corporates and selective high-yield amid credit spread tightening. This limited redemptions to 1.2% of AUM in fixed income, versus the peer average of 2.8% per Morningstar.

Market trends amplified these tailwinds. The S&P 500's 24% rally, powered by megacaps and AI enthusiasm, funneled $6.7 billion into our U.S. equity ETFs, with the Apex S&P 500 ETF capturing 3.2% market share in flows, behind only Vanguard's VOO and State Street's SPY. Our tech-enabled active ETFs, like the Apex AI Innovators ETF launched in Q2, drew $2.4 billion in retail inflows via Schwab and Fidelity. The fixed income rebound post-Fed pivot—with 10-year yields peaking at 5.25%—sparked $3.1 billion into short-duration and TIPS strategies as investors positioned for 75-100 basis points of 2024 rate cuts.

ESG and thematic trends were key, with sustainable investing now 22% of AUM, up from 16%, and $7.9 billion in full-year net inflows. The Apex Climate Transition Equity Fund, EU SFDR Article 8 compliant, attracted $1.5 billion from European wirehouses post-COP28 and amid U.S. SEC climate rules. Alternatives saw $2.3 billion quarterly, led by private credit; our evergreen private debt fund, seeded with $500 million from family offices, reached $4.2 billion AUM targeting 9-11% IRRs.

Regionally, the Americas drove 62% of inflows at $7.8 billion, boosted by retail platform stickiness—model portfolios on Betterment and Wealthfront generated $1.2 billion recurring flows. EMEA contributed $3.1 billion, up 35% YoY, via UCITS products amid MiFID II; we won UK DB pension mandates totaling £800 million. APAC shone with $1.6 billion or 13% of flows—double last year—through Hong Kong ETFs for Chinese investors via Stock Connect, and $450 million into yen-hedged equities as BOJ unwound yield curve control.

Our AlphaFlow AI platform, integrated across 70% of workflows, improved return forecasting by 15% in backtests, cutting flow volatility 20% during Q3 drawdowns. Fees held at 42 bps weighted average, versus industry drift to 38 bps, via ETF scale (35% AUM) and tax-loss harvesting adding 80 bps after-tax.

We guide to $50-55 billion net flows in 2024 on equity breadth, privates expansion, and 12 new launches like a semi-liquid infrastructure fund for 200 bps illiquidity premium. Risks like high rates or geopolitics loom, but our 60/40 active-passive mix and $15 billion dry powder ensure resilience. Institutional RFPs at $120 billion with 45% conversion underscore our multi-asset strength.

Turning to AUM growth and geographic mix, total AUM hit $1.45 trillion, up 14% YoY and 5% QoQ, outpacing industry 10% per PwC. Organic growth—net inflows plus market/FX excluding M&A—was 92% of expansion. Alternatives grew 22% to $320 billion on yield-seeking amid higher rates.

Geographically: North America at 52% or $754 billion, +16% YoY, on S&P 500 returns and $28 billion inflows; DC plans drove 40%, ETFs like APEXG ($45 billion) captured $12 billion. Pensions favored private credit Fund V ($15 billion commitments). Europe 28% or $406 billion, +11%, with $12 billion inflows into UCITS; Eurozone Climate fund €8 billion on SFDR. APAC 16% or $232 billion, +21%, $18 billion inflows; China Tech fund $25 billion, India ETF $4 billion. Rest of World 4% or $58 billion, +9%, with LatAm EM debt and ME SWFs $7 billion infrastructure.

Diversification—no region over 52%—de-risks us. Initiatives like $200 million distribution buildout, Alpha platform on 70% assets, semi-liquid alts sustain momentum to $1.7 trillion by 2025 at 4-6% flow margins, fees steady at 42 bps.

Before P&L details, our technology investments merit focus—a competitive moat. We spent $285 million on tech capex in FY2023, +22% YoY or 8% of opex, yielding 3.2x ROI and $42 billion flow uplift from digital acquisition/retention.

Client-facing: GAP WealthHub adoption hit 68% HNW/family offices, active users 1.2 million +31%, sessions 14 minutes +45%. Mirrors Aladdin but with ESG NLP. Institutional: Charles River OMS/TCA cut slippage 12 bps, $18 million alpha; Fireblocks blockchain custody $5 billion tokenized alts zero fails.

Data: 85% Snowflake migration for sub-second Monte Carlo; LLM sentiment on 40% equities +2.1% edge; SFDR ESG tracking 72% sustainable AUM. APAC $100 million mobile-first: WeChat +28% AUM to $180 billion, Grab/GoJek 15% millennial share. EMEA $75 million regtech: MiFID/Consumer Duty -19% compliance costs, 94% UK retention. Americas Envestnet RIA scaling +25% to $320 billion.

Positions for robo $25T by 2025, tokenized $16T illiquids 2030, advisor shortage via GAP Advisor Pro. RPA saved $92 million, 22% middle-office FTEs, SLAs 99.5%. FY2024 $320 million budget, 40% GenAI for flows/personalization.

On new products and rankings: Q2 launches tailored to inflation/geopolitics/AI. Apex Global Thematic Equity ETF (AGTHE) $450 million AUM, $320 million inflows +25% to projections, +12.4% since inception vs MSCI World ex-US via quant ML.

Apex Sustainable Multi-Asset Credit interval fund $1.2 billion, 60% pensions/insurers SFDR compliant, 7.8/10 MSCI score, 6-8% yield, $850 million inflows. EMEA Eurozone Equity Income UCITS €300 million first month; APAC China+ Hybrid Bond $200 million SWFs. +18% international AUM to $45 billion.

Rankings: 68% equity funds 4/5-star Morningstar, up from 62%; APGRX top decile +18.2% vs Russell +14.7% on tech overweight. 75% bonds top-quartile Lipper 3Y; APCBX 5-star +4.1% barbell. Real Assets #1 +11.5%. AlphaForge alternative data/NLP, tracking error <2%, IR 0.85 vs 0.45 median.

These drove $3.8 billion Q2 inflows, 55% performance-related. H2: longevity ETF, EM debt hedged. 10-12% organic growth at 45 bps fees.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Lisa. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in active equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by maintaining disciplined positioning in quality growth, private credit, and ESG themes while using our AlphaForge and AlphaFlow tools for edge. We launched the Apex Global Thematic Equity ETF this quarter, and early reception has been strong, with $450 million AUM and outperformance since inception.

Rachel Patel: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our equity and alternative funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by doubled flows in APAC via Hong Kong platforms and UCITS wins in Europe.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes deepening tech integrations, launching innovative products, and sustaining high client retention to drive long-term organic growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning. I wanted to dive into your client franchise metrics—specifically retention rates and new client acquisition. With AUM hitting $1.45 trillion this quarter, how are you thinking about organic growth sustainability amid fee compression and the passive juggernaut from Vanguard and BlackRock?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah, and thanks for joining the call. I'm happy to unpack our client retention and acquisition dynamics, which remain the bedrock of our organic AUM growth story at Apex Asset Management. In this industry, it's not just about inflows—it's about stickiness, win rates, and long-term relationships driving recurring revenue.

First, on client retention rates. We report a trailing 12-month rate of 97.8%, up 120 basis points year-over-year and above the peer average of 94% per Lipper. This is our 11th straight quarter above 97%, reflecting resilience in institutional, RIA, and HNW channels. Measured as beginning-of-period AUM retained net of redemptions, excluding lifecycle runoff.

Drivers include performance—active equities outperformed by 210 bps average in 2023 per Morningstar, large-cap growth by 450 bps net fees. Service via Client360 CRM with Aladdin risk analytics reduced multi-asset churn 15%; 92% departing clients cited no Apex issues. North America 98.5% anchored by pensions/endowments; EMEA 96.2% offset UK volatility with €12 billion UCITS; APAC 97.1% on SWF renewals, 25% alts share infrastructure debt.

On new client acquisition, 142 mandates $18.4 billion inflows Q4—strongest since 2021, +28% count, +35% dollars; organic growth 6.2% vs industry 4.1% Coalition Greenwich. 55% institutional $10.1B (78 wins), 30% RIA/HNW $5.5B, 15% retail $2.8B direct index. Win rates 42% from 38% on RFP tracker.

Catalysts: Q2 Alternatives Suite, $5B private credit 9-11% for insurers snagged Allianz/MetLife peers. ESG ETFs $3.2B retail, 12% sustainable equity creations on SFDR. $150 million ApexFlow AI lead scoring/Palantir shortened sales 22%, personalized pitches; new clients 15% more profitable digitally.

Positioning for barbell: active alts/quant to 20% AUM 2025, low-cost betas vs Vanguard. APAC Tokyo hub for $2T GPIF alts; EMEA Luxembourg ELTIFs retail. Guide 5-7% organic 2024, 97%+ retention, $50B pipeline 65% weighted; flows accelerate on rate peaks, $1.2B early from money markets.

Happy to take follow-ups.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you. And a follow-up on your technology investments and how they're impacting client acquisition?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Sarah. Our tech spend is yielding tangible results in acquisition and retention. As detailed, $285 million FY2023 drove 17% flow uplift. ApexFlow's AI lead scoring has shortened RIA cycles 22%, while WealthHub's 68% adoption boosts model portfolios. In APAC, WeChat/Grab integrations captured millennial flows, and regtech in EMEA enhanced compliance efficiency. These tools make us more scalable and profitable amid fee pressures.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Lee with JPMorgan.

Mike Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Global Equity Fund?

Michael Torres: Good morning, Mike. The Apex Global Equity Fund delivered 18.2% net returns for 2023, outperforming MSCI World by 420 bps, earning first-quartile Lipper rankings. This was driven by conviction in quality growth, including megacap tech positions hedged for concentration risk, supported by AlphaForge alternative data and NLP for edge. Institutional mandates flowed in response, and we see continued strength in 2024 breadth.

Mike Lee: And how is the new product Apex Global Thematic Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Rachel Patel: Thanks, Mike. AGTHE has exceeded expectations, reaching $450 million AUM with $320 million inflows since Q2 launch—25% above projections. +12.4% since inception net fees versus MSCI World ex-US, drawing retail and institutional via Schwab/Fidelity and wirehouses. Regional variants like Eurozone UCITS and China+ Bond are also ramping, fueling 18% international AUM growth. Early traction validates our glocal innovation.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
